draft.headline: Jake White's Fiji debut: a Tokyo rematch five weeks on
beats: Jake White coaches Fiji for the first time, appointed less than a year out from the World Cup in Australia. He inherits a side that has won 1 of 5 tests this year.
This is a rematch of the Pacific Nations Cup final on 19 September, on this same ground, where Japan won 20–15 to claim the title for the first time since 2019.
That result ended Fiji's run as two-time defending champions, after they had beaten Japan 33–27 in the 2025 final in Salt Lake City.

Japan bring three straight wins, including 63–14 over the USA and 57–12 over Canada. Fiji worked through systems in Nadi before sharpening combinations at D-Rocks in Japan for what they are billing as the Anniversary Test.

Any Fiji win lifts them to 9th, above Japan, and drops Japan below Fiji, Wales and Italy to 12th at best. A Japan win sends Fiji to 12th at best, while a draw changes neither side's rank. Both sides head to Europe on 7 November: Japan to Wales, Fiji to France.

draft.headline: Any Pumas win knocks Ireland out of world top three
beats: Ireland have been third in every world ranking since 13 July, but any Argentina win in Dublin drops them to fourth, below France. Win by 16 or more and Argentina also climb to seventh, above Australia.
The table is just as tight: Ireland are sixth on 10 points, level with Scotland in fifth, while Argentina sit eighth on 7, a point behind Australia.
Ireland have won 6 of 8 in 2026, but their last outing was a 21–40 loss to New Zealand on 18 July. Argentina have won 1 of 6, though they held Australia 28–28 on 5 September.
Andy Farrell's squad comes without captain Caelan Doris, still sidelined, and Jack Conan's shoulder needs further assessment after he went off against Clermont.
Ciaran Frawley is pressing his case after a flourishing display in Connacht's 45-36 Champions Cup win over Saracens.
Next up: Ireland host Fiji on 14 November, while Argentina travel to Italy.

draft.headline: Upset would lift Italy to 9th and topple the No.1 Boks
beats: The ranking swing is all one way. Any Italian win, or even a draw, lifts Italy from 12th to 9th, above Japan, Fiji and Wales, and drops South Africa to 2nd behind New Zealand. A Springbok win by any margin changes nothing.

Top-level international rugby returns to the Allianz Stadium in Turin for the visit of the reigning world champions. Their last meeting, on 15 November 2025, also on Italian soil, finished Italy 14–32 South Africa.

Italy arrive on four straight defeats, the latest 10–57 to Australia in July. They sit 11th of 12 in the Nations Championship without a point, level with Fiji. Their last win was 23–18 over England in March.
South Africa lead the table on 15 points, level with New Zealand and ahead on points difference. They took September's series against the All Blacks but lost their last outing 38–42 to Australia.
Victor Matfield expects Rassie Erasmus to test his depth this November. Matfield also warns against blooding too many youngsters at once, with France away on 13 November next.

draft.headline: Scotland's shot at 5th as the All Blacks hit Murrayfield
beats: Fifty-two weeks after Scotland lost 17–25 at home to New Zealand on 8 November 2025, the All Blacks return to a capacity 67,130 crowd at Scottish Gas Murrayfield. Mile world record-holder Josh Kerr will deliver the match ball.

New Zealand arrive hot: 50–19 and 43–21 over Australia after three straight defeats by South Africa. Beauden Barrett, 35, starred at full-back in Sydney, though Dave Rennie's injury list keeps mounting.
Scotland have not played since a five-try 33–17 win over Fiji on 18 July. They have won 5 of 8 in 2026, including a 47–38 shootout with Argentina, but were beaten 28–42 by South Africa.
In the Nations Championship, New Zealand sit 2nd, level on 15 points with South Africa. Scotland are 5th, locked on 10 with England and Ireland.
A Scotland win by any margin lifts them above England to 5th in the world, on 86.53 or 87.40 points. Lose by 16 or more and they slip below Australia to 7th. New Zealand stay 2nd whatever happens.

draft.headline: A point apart: Wales, Japan and a rankings swap in Cardiff
beats: Last time, on 15 November 2025, Wales edged Japan 24–23 at home. Fifty-one weeks on, the Brave Blossoms arrive in Cardiff ranked two places higher, 9th to Wales' 11th.

Form favours the visitors. Japan come in on three straight wins, capped by a 20–15 defeat of Fiji to claim the Pacific Nations Cup in September. Wales have lost two in a row, the last 0–43 to South Africa in July.
A Wales win by any margin lifts them to 9th, above Japan and Fiji, and drops Japan to 12th at best. A Japan win keeps them 9th and sends Wales below Italy, to 12th at best.
In the Nations Championship, a single point separates Wales (9th) and Japan (10th). Next up, Wales host New Zealand and Japan visit England.
Dewi Lake captains Steve Tandy's squad, which includes uncapped Dragons backs Che Hope and Aneurin Owen and Cardiff loosehead Rhys Barratt. Taulupe Faletau misses out.

draft.headline: Jake White's winless Fiji take on in-form France in Lyon
beats: Fiji have a new man in charge: World Cup-winning coach Jake White was appointed in October to lead them to next year's World Cup in Australia, with Warren Gatland reportedly missing out.
There's a French thread in this squad too: Virimi Vakatawa, who played for France at the 2019 World Cup, switched allegiance to Fiji in July.
Their last meeting, on 15 November 2025, also on French soil, ended France 34–21 Fiji.
Form is lopsided. France have won 6 of 8 this year, most recently 42–15 in Japan. Fiji have won 1 of 5, including an 8–73 loss to England, and lost 15–20 to Japan last time out.
A France win changes no ranking. A draw lifts Fiji to 9th above Japan. A Fiji win by 16 or more drops France to 6th, below England and Scotland.
In the Nations Championship, France sit 3rd, two points clear of England, before hosting South Africa on 13 November. Fiji are bottom, level with Italy on zero.

issues.claim: Headline: "Jake White's winless Fiji take on in-form France in Lyon"
issues.problem: Fiji are not winless in 2026. The Form list shows a 45–29 home win over Canada on 2026-09-12 (Pacific Nations Cup), so they have won 1 of 5 this year. They are winless only in the Nations Championship (W0 in 3 games).

draft.headline: Wallabies win would vault them past England into 5th
beats: The ranking swap is live. Any Australia win lifts them to 5th, above England and Scotland, and drops England to 7th. An England win keeps both sides where they are.
England won the last meeting 25–7 at home on 1 November 2025.

England arrive on two straight wins, 73–8 in Fiji and 31–24 in Argentina, though they have won only 3 of 8 in 2026. Australia have just lost to New Zealand twice, 19–50 and 21–43, after beating South Africa 42–38 in September.
In the Nations Championship, England sit 4th, two points behind France and level with Scotland. Australia are 7th, two adrift of Ireland and a point clear of Argentina, with Scotland away next.

Former England prop Dan Cole fears the Prem's style could leave Steve Borthwick's side exposed in November. Victor Matfield has set out what the Wallabies need to be a top-five team again, and a win here would put them 5th.
